# apple-container

## virtualisation.apple-container.enable

Whether to enable Apple’s container runtime (apple/container). The runtime is per-user:
it runs as launchd user agents of `system.primaryUser`, so it is
up only while that user is logged in. Requires macOS 15+ on Apple
Silicon.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
false
```

*Example:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)

## virtualisation.apple-container.network

Networks to create, as `container network create`. Never
updated or deleted: delete one to have it recreated with new
settings. Container-to-container networking requires macOS 26+.

*Type:*
attribute set of (submodule)

*Default:*

```nix
{ }
```

*Example:*

```nix
{
  v6 = {
    subnetV6 = "fd12:3456:789a::/64";
  };
}
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)

## virtualisation.apple-container.socktainer.enable

Whether to enable socktainer, a Docker-compatible API socket on top of the runtime. Requires macOS 26+.

*Type:*
boolean

*Default:*

```nix
true
```

*Example:*

```nix
true
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)

## virtualisation.apple-container.socktainer.package

The socktainer package. It talks to the runtime as a `container`

*Type:*
package

## virtualisation.apple-container.socktainer.socketPath

Where socktainer listens. Bind-mount it into a container at

## virtualisation.apple-container.system.dns.defaultDomain

The domain containers are registered under, so that the host
resolves `<container>.<defaultDomain>`. The runtime has a single
default domain, for all of the user’s containers.

The module owns the primary user’s
`~/.config/container/config.toml` to set it (`[dns] domain`);
null leaves that file alone.

*Type:*
null or string

*Default:*

```nix
"container"
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)

## virtualisation.apple-container.system.kernel

The default guest kernel per architecture (`arm64` or `amd64`), as
`container system kernel set`. A bare string is the tar,
with the Kata Containers layout.

Empty installs the runtime’s recommended kernel on first start. A
changed kernel replaces the installed one (`--force`). A container
can boot its own kernel instead, with
`virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.apple-container.kernel`.

*Type:*
attribute set of ((submodule) or string convertible to it)

*Default:*

```nix
{ }
```

*Example:*

```nix
{ arm64 = { tar = "${pkgs.apple-container-kernel}/kernel.tar"; binary = "./vmlinux-arm64"; }; }

```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)

## virtualisation.apple-container.volumesRoot

Directory to hold the primary user’s volumes instead of
`~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.container/volumes`,
e.g. to keep them off the internal disk.

Activation symlinks the volumes directory to it, only while the
volumes directory is absent or empty; otherwise it warns and leaves
it alone. Under `/Volumes/<name>`, it must be a subdirectory of
the volume, and nothing happens while the volume is unmounted.
Unsetting it leaves an existing symlink in place.

*Type:*
null or absolute path not in the Nix store

*Default:*

```nix
null
```

*Example:*

```nix
"/Volumes/Virtual Machines/container-volumes"
```

*Declared by:*

- [\<nixham/modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix>](../../../modules/nix-darwin/virtualisation/apple-container/default.nix)
